detail: runtime.test.ts > position > clamps negative and non-finite input to the start: AssertionError: expected false to be true (position(TABATA, Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY).isComplete)
error: runtime.test.ts > position > clamps negative and non-finite input to the start: AssertionError: expected false to be true (position(TABATA, Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY).isComplete)
fix: Kept the implementation and corrected the test: ALL non-finite input (NaN, -Infinity, +Infinity) clamps to the start. One rule for invalid input beats two special cases, and a real monotonic clock never produces these values. Documented the rule in the test and in position()'s doc comment.
root_cause: Test expectation was wrong, not the implementation. position() guards with `Number.isFinite(elapsedMs) ? Math.max(0, elapsedMs) : 0`, so +Infinity is rejected as invalid input and clamps to 0 rather than being read as 'past the end' and completing the workout.

detail: Idle run screen rendered the 'Ready' panel AND a live countdown simultaneously, putting 4 children into a 3-row grid
error: Idle run screen rendered the 'Ready' panel AND a live countdown simultaneously, putting 4 children into a 3-row grid
fix: Derive `const isRunning = status === 'running' || status === 'paused'` and gate on `isRunning ? at.entry : null`. Same flag unlights the effort strip when idle (currentIndex -1).
root_cause: position(timeline, 0) legitimately returns the FIRST entry, not null — only completion yields a null entry. So `at.entry` is truthy before the workout starts, and gating the running body on `entry &&` alone was true during 'idle'.

detail: Skipping a step while paused (or stepping back from complete) left the clock advancing, so the next Resume credited a huge bogus pause and jumped the workout forward
error: Skipping a step while paused (or stepping back from complete) left the clock advancing, so the next Resume credited a huge bogus pause and jumped the workout forward
fix: seekTo takes an explicit `freeze` flag (`status !== 'running'`) and always sets pausedAt accordingly. Also extracted the whole arithmetic into pure src/state/clock.ts (Clock + elapsed/started/paused/resumed/seeked) with 11 unit tests that need no DOM — including one named for this bug.
root_cause: seekTo() re-anchored startedAt but only refreshed pausedAt if it was already non-zero. Stepping back from 'complete' set status to 'paused' while pausedAt stayed 0, so readElapsed() kept using now() — the clock ran while the UI said paused, and resume() then added (now - 0).

detail: max-height: 40cqh on the media panel had no container to resolve against
error: max-height: 40cqh on the media panel had no container to resolve against
fix: Use `min(40svh, 26rem)` explicitly. Rule: with container-type: inline-size, only cqi/cqw are meaningful.
root_cause: `.run` declares `container-type: inline-size`, which establishes an INLINE-axis query container only. cqh needs `container-type: size` (which requires a definite block size). With no eligible container, cqh silently falls back to the small viewport — right by accident, wrong by intent.

detail: USER REPORTED: 'the countdown and image panels need to be responsive and size to occupy the available screen space. they're tiny on my laptop'
error: USER REPORTED: 'the countdown and image panels need to be responsive and size to occupy the available screen space. they're tiny on my laptop'
fix: Named containers (`shell` / inline-size for layout switching, `body` / size on .run__body so BOTH axes are queryable — safe because a 1fr row of a 100%-height grid has a definite block size). Countdown is now max(3rem, min(calc(84cqi / var(--chars)), 52cqh)) with --chars set from the string's em width (digit 1, colon 0.5) so '8' and '17' match while '4:30' steps down. Columns became minmax(0, 3fr) minmax(0, 2fr); the panel frame drops aspect-ratio on wide layouts and stretches to the row height with object-fit: contain.
root_cause: Both were capped in rem, so a big screen was wasted. `.count__clock` was clamp(5rem, 34cqi, 15rem) — on a 1440px laptop 34cqi computes to ~490px and the 15rem ceiling chopped it to 240px. The media column was minmax(16rem, 22rem), hard-capped at 352px. Neither considered available HEIGHT at all, and `.run` was container-type: inline-size so cqh was not even available.

detail: USER REPORTED: 'make all the small text much bigger' — labels, meta rows, button text and stats were unreadable
error: USER REPORTED: 'make all the small text much bigger' — labels, meta rows, button text and stats were unreadable
fix: --label-size is now clamp(1rem, 1.6cqi, 1.6rem), so ~11px became 16px on a phone and 23px on a laptop; tracking eased to 0.11em since the same tracking reads much wider at a larger size. Also enlarged: exercise name floor 1.25rem -> 1.75rem, stat figures to clamp(1.75rem, 4cqi, 3rem), primary button its own clamp(1.05rem, 1.9cqi, 1.9rem), chevron glyphs their own larger scale, button targets 56px -> 64px (primary 76px).
root_cause: The --label token was `600 0.7rem/1.2` (~11.2px) with 0.16em tracking — a sensible size for a desktop dashboard, and a deliberate typographic counterweight to the giant numerals, but it ignored this app's actual requirement: readable across a gym, mid-effort, at 2-3 metres. Fixed rem sizing also meant it never grew on a large screen.

detail: Control row would overflow a phone width once button text was enlarged (5 buttons, primary min-width 12rem, no wrapping)
error: Control row would overflow a phone width once button text was enlarged (5 buttons, primary min-width 12rem, no wrapping)
fix: Added `flex-wrap: wrap` so transport controls take the first line and Reset/Sound fall to the second, and changed the primary button to `min-width: min(12rem, 100%)` so a narrow screen cannot be forced wider than it is.
root_cause: `.controls` was a nowrap flex row with `justify-content: center`, and `.btn--primary` had a fixed `min-width: 12rem`. At the enlarged label size the five buttons total ~550px against a 390px phone. Latent before the type change; the bigger text made it certain.

detail: USER REPORTED: 'the progress bar on top - the muted red bars look brown'
error: USER REPORTED: 'the progress bar on top - the muted red bars look brown'
fix: Dropped opacity for explicit per-state backgrounds. Upcoming steps are neutral `var(--ink-600)` — their HEIGHT already encodes work vs rest, so hue was redundant. Completed steps keep hue but mix toward a LIGHT grey rather than down toward black: `color-mix(in oklab, var(--step-colour) 55%, var(--bone-dim))`, giving #C9716D for red. Only the current step is at full strength.
root_cause: The effort strip used a single background colour with opacity per state (0.22 todo / 0.5 done / 1 current) over a near-black ground. Compositing a saturated hue down toward black is exactly how you make brown: red #EF4A3F at 22% resolves to #431F1D and at 50% to #802E2A. Green and blue muddied the same way, but red is the one that reads unmistakably as brown because dark desaturated red IS brown.

detail: USER REPORTED (with screenshot): 'the countdown numbers are not centered'
error: USER REPORTED (with screenshot): 'the countdown numbers are not centered'
fix: Hoisted the value into `--tracking` and added `padding-right: calc(-1 * var(--tracking))` on the block. Narrowing the content box by the same amount shifts the centred line back by exactly half of it. Kept as one variable so the two can never drift apart.
root_cause: CSS applies letter-spacing after EVERY character including the last, so with `letter-spacing: -0.045em` the line box is narrower than the visible glyphs by that amount. Centring the line box therefore leaves the glyphs offset by half of it — about 20px at a 459px font size, and visibly off next to the centred exercise name and meta row.

detail: USER REPORTED: 'when the number of digits reduces, the numbers get bigger pushing the rest of the content off the screen'
error: USER REPORTED: 'when the number of digits reduces, the numbers get bigger pushing the rest of the content off the screen'
fix: clockWidth now returns Math.max(2, units), so the size only ever steps DOWN for longer strings. Test corrected to assert the floor, plus a new test asserting the sequence is monotonically non-increasing.
root_cause: clockWidth() returned the literal em width of the string, so a single digit gave 1 and the font size became `coef * 1cqi / 1` instead of `/ 2`. The width term then stopped binding, the height term took over, and '9' rendered up to 100% larger than '10' — measured +100% at 342x710, +73% at 342x560, +59% at 600x900. The coefficient had been calibrated for two digits all along. A test even asserted clockWidth('8') === 1 under the name 'sizes one and two digits so the countdown does not jump', so the test guaranteed the very jump its name denied.

detail: Media panel pushed below the fold on a short narrow window (visible in the same screenshot — no image panel at all)
error: Media panel pushed below the fold on a short narrow window (visible in the same screenshot — no image panel at all)
fix: Dropped aspect-ratio and max-height entirely; the frame is `height: 100%` in both layouts. `.run__body` stacked is now `grid-template-rows: auto minmax(0, 1fr)` so the countdown block takes what it needs and the panel absorbs the remainder. Also gave the clock its own `--clock-height` per layout: 40cqh stacked (the panel needs room below), 74cqh beside the panel. object-fit: contain means a smaller frame never distorts the image.
root_cause: In the stacked layout the panel frame had `aspect-ratio: 4/3` with `max-height: min(40svh, 26rem)`, so it demanded a height proportional to its WIDTH regardless of how much vertical space was left. Countdown + name + meta + a 4:3 panel simply exceeds a short body, and the overflow went off-screen silently.

detail: USER REPORTED: 'the text on the cards is the wrong way around - the routine name should be bigger and the text below it smaller'
error: USER REPORTED: 'the text on the cards is the wrong way around - the routine name should be bigger and the text below it smaller'
fix: Moved `.label` and `.unit` to theme.css (loaded first by main.tsx, so components can override) and rewrote them with LONGHAND properties, so setting font-size or the --label-size token actually wins. `.row__meta` now steps down via `--label-size: var(--label-size-sm)`. Name/meta ratio is 1.5-2.07x depending on width.
root_cause: `.label` was declared as `font: var(--label)` — the FONT SHORTHAND, which resets font-size. It lived in run-screen.css while `.row__meta` (which carries both classes) set its own smaller font-size in library.css. Equal specificity, so source order decided, and App.tsx imports LibraryScreen before RunScreen — so run-screen.css loaded last and `.label` silently clobbered the card's size. Card meta rendered at 44.5px against a 30.4px routine name on a laptop, inverted at every width.

detail: USER REPORTED: 'something is off with the combination of fonts - the home screen seems different to the routine screens'
error: USER REPORTED: 'something is off with the combination of fonts - the home screen seems different to the routine screens'
fix: One scale in theme.css: three tracking tokens keyed to ROLE (--track-display -0.03em, --track-name -0.01em, --label-tracking 0.11em) and four size tokens (--size-display, --size-title, --size-name, --label-size plus --label-size-sm). Both stylesheets now reference tokens only; the sole remaining literal is .count__name, which needs a cqh term the tokens do not carry, and is commented as such.
root_cause: No shared type scale. An audit found 11 ad-hoc font-size expressions and 5 different letter-spacing values (-0.03, -0.02, -0.01, 0.06, 0.1, 0.11em) split across library.css and run-screen.css, each invented per element. The same role was styled differently per screen — uppercase labels tracked 0.06em on one and 0.11em on the other, and screen titles used unrelated sizes — so the two screens read as different apps.

detail: USER REPORTED: the next-up line sits flush against the controls divider; a 3px nudge appeared to do nothing
error: USER REPORTED: the next-up line sits flush against the controls divider; a 3px nudge appeared to do nothing
fix: Gave the stacked body `var(--step-4)` (16px) bottom padding and removed the 3px margin as redundant. Fixing the missing padding rather than stacking a nudge on top of a zero.
root_cause: `.run__body` in the STACKED layout had `padding: var(--step-5) var(--step-5) 0` — zero bottom padding — so the panel's bottom edge met the controls' border-top directly. The 3px margin DID apply (measurable as ~6 device px at 2x in the screenshot), it was simply the entire clearance that existed. The wide layout was fine because it has 24px bottom padding.

detail: USER REPORTED: 'the sound after the 3s countdown is supposed to sound like a bell but it sounds like a click'
error: USER REPORTED: 'the sound after the 3s countdown is supposed to sound like a bell but it sounds like a click'
fix: Note gained `sustain` (fraction of peak the strike falls to) and `strikeMs`, so the envelope is attack -> strike -> long tail. Bell is now sustain 0.33, strikeMs 22, durationMs 2050, with the inharmonic partial given decayScale 0.45 because high partials die before the body stops ringing. And `pending` became a Map of node -> scheduled start time, so `cancelPending` skips anything already sounding and only drops future cues.
root_cause: TWO causes. (1) The envelope was a single exponential from peak, which is loud in the middle and silent by 500ms. Re-measuring the app's bell showed the real shape is a STRIKE plus a RING: it drops to 0.33 of peak within 25ms and is still audible at 1200ms. A single exponential is a tone being switched off; the quiet long tail is what makes it a bell. (2) `cancelPending()` stopped EVERY tracked oscillator including ones already sounding, and the scheduler re-arms its window every 10 seconds — so any cue overlapping a re-arm was cut off mid-ring, which is itself an audible click. With phase changes every 10-20s in a Tabata, collisions were frequent.

detail: First FFT pass reported six 'partials' for each cue that were really adjacent bins of two peaks
error: First FFT pass reported six 'partials' for each cue that were really adjacent bins of two peaks
fix: Re-ran peak-picking with a 40Hz minimum separation and reported relative magnitudes, which confirmed the bell is genuinely just 2659Hz at 1.00 and 6854Hz at 0.39.
root_cause: Took the top-6 spectral bins by magnitude with no minimum separation, so spectral leakage around a single peak filled the list (511/517/519/527/529/531 Hz is one tone, not six). It happened to identify the right two partials for the bell, but it could easily have missed a weaker lower fundamental.

detail: USER REPORTED: 'the countdown is still changing size when it transitions from 1:00 to 59 and squashing the image'
error: USER REPORTED: 'the countdown is still changing size when it transitions from 1:00 to 59 and squashing the image'
fix: `--chars` now comes from the step's LONGEST string — clockWidth(clock(ceil(entry.durationMs / 1000))) — so it is constant for the whole step and the countdown cannot change size while running. And the stacked split is fixed proportions (56fr / 44fr) instead of auto, so the image never moves. Because the countdown now only gets 56% of the body while cqh still measures the whole body, --clock-height came down from 40cqh to 34cqh; verified the count block fits its row at six window sizes including 342x380.
root_cause: TWO causes, both left over from bug-010's partial fix. (1) `--chars` was computed from the CURRENT clock string, so a step counting through the minute boundary went from '1:00' (3.5 units) to '59' (2 units) and the font grew ~75% mid-step. Flooring at 2 had only fixed the single-digit case. (2) The stacked layout used `grid-template-rows: auto minmax(0, 1fr)`, so the countdown block took whatever height it needed and the image absorbed the rest — meaning any change in numeral size resized the picture.

detail: USER REPORTED: 'on a small screen can you shrink the image to fit the available space?'
error: USER REPORTED: 'on a small screen can you shrink the image to fit the available space?'
fix: Two viewport-height tiers hand space to the image on short screens: at <=700px the split becomes 50/50 with --clock-height 28cqh, and at <=540px it becomes 46/54 with 22cqh plus lower name and label FLOORS (those floors, not the countdown, are what crowd the row at that height). Image renders 19-47% larger depending on size; a normal phone portrait (390x844) is unchanged. Declared before the wide container block, since the two-column layout overrides both rows and --clock-height and must not be affected.
root_cause: Not an overflow — the image was already contained. The exercise illustrations are near-square (876x800 measured from the real file), so a SHORT WIDE frame fits them to its height and leaves the width unused: at a 342x103 frame the picture rendered at 0.13x, tiny inside a large empty bordered box. The fixed 56/44 stacked split gave the panel the same share regardless of how little vertical space there was.

detail: USER REPORTED (screenshot): the exercise image is vertically truncated — the bottom of the picture is cut off at the frame edge
error: USER REPORTED (screenshot): the exercise image is vertically truncated — the bottom of the picture is cut off at the frame edge
fix: The image is absolutely positioned with `inset: 0` inside a `position: relative` frame. An absolutely-positioned box takes its dimensions from the containing block directly, so the height is definite regardless of the grid, and contain then shrinks the picture to fit — full height, letterboxed at the sides.
root_cause: `.panel__frame img` had `width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: contain`, but as a normal grid item its `height: 100%` was resolving to AUTO. The box therefore took the image's natural aspect at full width (463x423 for an 876x800 image in a 463px frame), grew taller than the frame's 295px, and `overflow: hidden` cut the bottom off. `object-fit: contain` never letterboxed anything, because the box it was fitting into was already too tall. I had twice reasoned that 'contain means it cannot overflow' — which is only true once the box itself is bounded.

detail: USER REPORTED: 'the save button is invisible' (editor header)
error: USER REPORTED: 'the save button is invisible' (editor header)
fix: Gave `--phase` a root default of `var(--role-rest)` in theme.css; the run screen still overrides it per step. Also moved `.btn*` and `.chip*` out of run-screen.css / library.css into theme.css, since three screens use them and they only worked from a screen-specific file because the bundler concatenates all CSS.
root_cause: `.btn--primary` is `color: var(--ink-900); background: var(--phase)`, and `--phase` was only ever set as an inline style on `.run`. In the editor it is undefined, and an undefined custom property makes the whole `background` declaration INVALID at computed-value time — so the background fell back to transparent and the button rendered as dark text on a dark ground.

detail: USER REPORTED: 'the fourth sound after a round is also broken like the other one was' — the workout-complete figure was truncated
error: USER REPORTED: 'the fourth sound after a round is also broken like the other one was' — the workout-complete figure was truncated
fix: Cancellation is judged per CUE, not per note: every oscillator is tagged with the moment its cue began, and a cue that has begun is left entirely alone including its remaining notes. Added a 0.15s grace so tick-versus-audio-clock skew cannot cancel a figure a hair before it starts, and added deduplication in the scheduler (keyed `kind@atMs`) so a spared cue cannot be re-queued by the next arm and played twice.
root_cause: The completion cue is SEVEN notes spread over ~3.45s, queued as separate oscillators at future times. It fires at exactly totalMs — the same instant the timer sets status to 'complete', which re-runs the scheduler effect and called cancelPending(). The earlier fix spared oscillators whose OWN start time had passed, so the first note survived and every later note of the same figure was stopped. Per-note reasoning fixed the single-note bell and left the multi-note fanfare broken in exactly the same way.

detail: USER REPORTED: the image placeholder text is truncated on a portrait iPad
error: USER REPORTED: the image placeholder text is truncated on a portrait iPad
fix: Padding is proportional on both axes (`4cqh 4cqi`), so the available share is a constant 92% at any size. The coefficient is now an explicit budget over an explicit advance — 84 of the 92 available, divided by a 0.72em advance — and the gap between 84 and 92 is where all the safety lives, because the sizing maths is exact by construction. Added `overflow-wrap: anywhere` so a wider-than-assumed font breaks a word rather than clipping it, and a test asserting the fit holds against a PESSIMISTIC 0.78em advance, since testing against the assumed advance would prove nothing.
root_cause: `fitCqi`'s coefficient was 161, derived as 100 / 0.62 — two optimistic assumptions compounded. Bold uppercase advances nearer 0.68-0.72em, not 0.62, and the calculation used the FULL container width while `.panel__empty` had 12px of fixed padding either side. On a portrait iPad the wide layout gives the panel only ~250px, where 24px of padding is a tenth of the width, so every fallback name overflowed by about 20% and was clipped by the frame's overflow: hidden. It fitted on a laptop purely because the panel is twice as wide there and the padding proportionally trivial.

detail: Tinted library rows lost their hover feedback entirely
error: Tinted library rows lost their hover feedback entirely
fix: Added an explicit tinted-hover rule mixing the same wash into the lighter --ink-700 ground. Delete-confirm is excluded from the tint via :not() rather than by source order.
root_cause: `.row[data-clickable='true']:hover` sets a flat `background`, and the new `.row[data-colour]:not([data-confirming='true'])` tint rule TIES with it on specificity. Source order alone decided it, and the tint came later, so hover never applied to a coloured row.

detail: A truncated download was read as a genuinely smaller image (179KB vs 477KB)
error: A truncated download was read as a genuinely smaller image (179KB vs 477KB)
fix: Re-downloaded with an explicit --max-time inside the command budget and decoded before comparing.
root_cause: A curl hit the 2-minute command timeout and left a partial PNG. Its size and sha256 were then compared as evidence, making two identical images look very different. PIL exposed it: 'image file is truncated'.

detail: imageCatalogue.ts claimed duplicate-named images were 'genuinely different images'
error: imageCatalogue.ts claimed duplicate-named images were 'genuinely different images'
fix: Removed both duplicates (27 images), corrected the comment to state what was measured, repointed 6 references in two seeded routines at the canonical URL, added two guard tests.
root_cause: The claim was written when the file was created and never checked. Both pairs are re-uploads of one photograph: aligned for a 1px crop they differ 1.8/255 and 3.3/255 mean, where genuinely different plates differ 16.6/255.

detail: Rattle rate reported as SLOWING to 9.6Hz when the time axis was compressed
error: Rattle rate reported as SLOWING to 9.6Hz when the time axis was compressed
fix: Measure the final tiled 700ms curve, and return NaN when the window is under 250ms rather than guessing. Peak-count measure deleted with a comment recording why. FFT validated by tracking RATTLE proportionally across x1.18/x1.32/x1.48.
root_cause: Compressing time can only raise a modulation rate. The FFT window was the ~127ms compressed steady portion, too short to resolve 18Hz from 24Hz, so it locked onto an envelope component. A peak-counting cross-check was wrong twice too (115Hz, then 48Hz, against a true 18Hz) because one rattle cycle has several local maxima.

detail: Committed generator could not run from the repo: FileNotFoundError 'amp.npy'
error: Committed generator could not run from the repo: FileNotFoundError 'amp.npy'
fix: Paths resolved relative to __file__, ANALYSIS_DIR override, and a real error message instead of a numpy traceback. scripts/.analysis/ gitignored because full-rate amplitude+frequency of the Tabata mp3 is effectively a copy of it.
root_cause: Hardcoded bare input filenames and an absolute output path, so it only ran from the scratchpad it was written in.

detail: Large gap between the 'Routine text' label and its textarea in the paste dialog
error: Large gap between the 'Routine text' label and its textarea in the paste dialog
fix: grid-template-rows: auto minmax(0, 1fr) on .paste__field - label sized to its text, control taking the rest.
root_cause: Both children of .paste__field were auto grid rows, and a grid stretches auto tracks to absorb spare height, so the label's row grew with the dialog and left the label at the top of it.

detail: Paste dialog looked bottom-heavy: too much space above the buttons
error: Paste dialog looked bottom-heavy: too much space above the buttons
fix: Three explicit tracks with the rest implicit, so there are exactly as many tracks as children.
root_cause: grid-template-rows declared five tracks but the dialog has four children when the parse report is absent, and an empty explicit track still takes its gap.

detail: Confirm dialog rendered nearly full-height, with its two buttons stretched into 280px slabs
error: Confirm dialog rendered nearly full-height, with its two buttons stretched into 280px slabs
fix: height: fit-content plus align-self: center and align-content: center on .notice so the rows pack; align-items: center on .notice__actions so the chips keep their own height.
root_cause: A dialog is a DOM child of the full-height grid screen that opened it. Stretched by that grid, .notice's three auto rows split the spare height between them - title pinned to the top, detail marooned in the middle, buttons at the bottom - and .notice__actions, being a stretched flex container, pulled its chips to full height as well.

detail: On a short narrow window the step name pushed 'Step 8 / 179' out of the count column and behind the media panel
error: On a short narrow window the step name pushed 'Step 8 / 179' out of the count column and behind the media panel
fix: A --name-lines custom property, set from nameLines(entry.name), subtracts 11cqh from the clock's cap for every line past the first - in the stacked layout and the two-column one. .count's lead track is minmax(0, 1fr) so it can shrink.
root_cause: The countdown and the step name share one column but were sized independently: the clock claimed 34cqh and a two-line name another 22cqh, more than the 56fr row holds. .count's lead track was a bare 1fr, whose min-content floor meant the grid grew past its parent row rather than giving way, so the meta row landed under the panel below.

detail: Exporting a pasted routine and re-importing it silently dropped it: 'no readable routines'
error: Exporting a pasted routine and re-importing it silently dropped it: 'no readable routines'
fix: isBlock accepts every kind in GROUP_KINDS (repeat, ladder, section) and validates their children. Round-trip test added over a real pasted routine.
root_cause: isBlock is a WHITELIST - it accepted only 'segment' and 'repeat'. When ladders and sections were added it was not updated, so isWorkout rejected every pasted routine and fromBundle's .filter(isWorkout) discarded it. The export itself wrote the routine out perfectly, so the backup looked valid and restored nothing.

detail: The first whistle of a workout — the one at the end of the get-ready — played the plain 2900Hz fallback tone instead of the recording
error: The first whistle of a workout — the one at the end of the get-ready — played the plain 2900Hz fallback tone instead of the recording
fix: Two parts. (1) samples.ts starts the download at module load and exposes sampleBytes() — the network is the slow half and needs no AudioContext, so it does not wait for the gesture. (2) engine.onSampleDecoded() notifies when a buffer lands; the scheduler cancels pending, forgets the keys requeueable() says were actually dropped, and re-arms. requeueable() shares CANCEL_GRACE_MS with cancelPending so a cue already sounding is spared rather than queued twice.
root_cause: A cue is BUILT when it is scheduled, not when it sounds: playNote reads this.samples.get(name) at schedule time and creates either a buffer source or the synthesised fallback there and then. unlock() starts the whistle fetch+decode without awaiting it, and useCueScheduler's first arm() runs synchronously in the same tick, queueing the whole 30s lookahead window before the bytes could possibly land. Dedup via `scheduled` then means those cues are never revisited, so every whistle in the first half-minute kept the fallback. It only looked intermittent because any clock mutation (pause, resume, skip, seek) bumps `generation`, which clears the dedup set and requeues with the recording.

detail: Choosing images for two steps in a row shared ONE undo step — one press of undo took both pictures back
error: Choosing images for two steps in a row shared ONE undo step — one press of undo took both pictures back
fix: history.push now takes the FIELD being typed into (string | null) instead of a boolean, and only replaces the present when the field matches. isTypedPatch (editor/blocks.ts) names the only keystroke-by-keystroke field on a step — name — so media, role, note and alternative are discrete. The timing NUMBER box now coalesces (it is typed) while the unit select stays discrete.
root_cause: patchSegment passed `coalesce = patch.role === undefined`, i.e. 'anything that is not the role is text'. A media patch from the picker, the upload or the link field therefore coalesced, and history.push replaces the present when the previous push was also coalescible. So a second image pick overwrote the first entry, and any image pick following a typing run was absorbed into it. The coalescing flag was also a single global boolean, so typing in two different fields collapsed together.

detail: Focusing the image link field of a step with an uploaded photo and tabbing away deleted the photo; blurring an unchanged note left an undo step that undid nothing
error: Focusing the image link field of a step with an uploaded photo and tabbing away deleted the photo; blurring an unchanged note left an undo step that undid nothing
fix: commitText returns when the trimmed value matches what is stored. commitUrl clears only when the media is source 'remote', returns on an unrecognised link, and writes only when the normalised URL differs from the current one. The new × in the field is the deliberate way to remove any image, including an uploaded one.

detail: User-reported: after starting a routine by CLICKING play, the right arrow key did not skip — starting it with the spacebar and the arrows worked
error: User-reported: after starting a routine by CLICKING play, the right arrow key did not skip — starting it with the spacebar and the arrows worked
fix: Extracted `shortcutApplies(tagName, key)` to src/ui/keys.ts: a field or select takes every key, a button takes only Space and Enter (which activate it), and the arrows / m / k always belong to the screen. Tested without a DOM.

Clicking a control leaves it focused, so every later keydown targets a <button> and EVERY shortcut was dropped, arrows included. detail: User-reported (iPhone, installed to the home screen): the top of the screen sits behind the camera indent, and the run screen's back button cannot be tapped while a routine is running
error: User-reported (iPhone, installed to the home screen): the top of the screen sits behind the camera indent, and the run screen's back button cannot be tapped while a routine is running

The unclickable back button is the same cause rather than a second bug: iOS consumes touches in the status bar region, so a control there is not merely clipped, it is unreachable.

detail: User-reported with a screenshot (iPhone, home-screen install): the time remaining collided with the step name, and a large empty band sat below the controls
error: User-reported with a screenshot (iPhone, home-screen install): the time remaining collided with the step name, and a large empty band sat below the controls

(1) `html, body, #root { height: 100% }` — on an iOS standalone install with viewport-fit=cover, a PERCENTAGE height resolves against the safe viewport (screen minus the 59pt status-bar strip) while the page paints under the island, so the app's box ended 59pt above the bottom of the screen. detail: User-reported with a screenshot (iOS, list mode): some groups rendered with names broken mid-word — 'Spe / ed / Ska / ters' — while other groups looked fine
error: User-reported with a screenshot (iOS, list mode): some groups rendered with names broken mid-word — 'Spe / ed / Ska / ters' — while other groups looked fine
fix: Added the width term the sizing was missing: min(32cqh / --lines, 6.5cqi), which leaves the name about 7em once both fixed columns and the padding have taken their share. The qualifier may now also wrap (nowrap removed), so it is compressible rather than the name being whatever is left.
root_cause: `.sheet__list` sized its rows from the HEIGHT budget only — `clamp(1.05rem, 32cqh / var(--lines), 2.25rem)`. A row is three grid columns and two are fixed in em (the count at 3.4em and the per-side qualifier at 0.72em with white-space: nowrap), so a bigger font leaves the name column less width. With only three or four exercises the height term hit the 2.25rem ceiling; at that size the fixed columns took most of the row and `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on the name broke words a character at a time. It only happened to groups containing a per-side row, because that column collapses to nothing otherwise — which is why some groups looked fine.

detail: User-reported: New routine, Duplicate routine and paste-import did nothing on laptop, iPhone and iPad alike
error: User-reported: New routine, Duplicate routine and paste-import did nothing on laptop, iPhone and iPad alike

detail: User-reported on iOS and iPadOS: dialogs rendered nearly full-height with the title at the top, the detail in the middle, the buttons at the bottom, and Close drawn as a tall slab
error: User-reported on iOS and iPadOS: dialogs rendered nearly full-height with the title at the top, the detail in the middle, the buttons at the bottom, and Close drawn as a tall slab
fix: Two elements. `.modal` is a transparent sheet filling the viewport whose job is to centre a panel inside the safe area (and to carry overscroll-behavior: contain, so the screen behind cannot move). The panel is a plain div with the ground, border, padding and rows, and `align-content: start` so rows hug. Applied to the notice, confirm, paste and picker dialogs; the lightbox was already a sheet and only needed the insets.
root_cause: The panel WAS the <dialog>, held to its content by `height: fit-content` plus `align-self: center` and `align-content: center`. On iOS that box takes the height available instead of hugging, and the implicit auto rows then stretch (align-content: normal behaves as stretch in grid) to share out the spare height. Removing align-content made the stretch obvious; keeping it made the content overflow a scroll container upward so the title was clipped. Both symptoms, one wrong premise.

detail: User-reported: "Let's go!" did not play on the first routine started after opening the app, and worked on every start after that
error: User-reported: "Let's go!" did not play on the first routine started after opening the app, and worked on every start after that
fix: `unlockSpeech()` in speech.ts speaks a single space at zero volume, called synchronously from every control alongside `audio.unlock()` — the same problem the AudioContext has and the same shape of answer. Idempotent, inaudible, and it leaves nothing queued for the first real line to cancel.
root_cause: iOS drops the FIRST utterance a page makes unless `speak()` is called inside a user gesture. The opening line is fired from a React effect and then a setTimeout (AFTER_START_CUE_MS), so it is never itself in the gesture — the tap is over by the time it runs. The first attempt was therefore swallowed, and it also served as the page's first utterance, which is why every later line was audible.

detail: User-reported: on an iPad in portrait the run screen placed the countdown and the media panel side by side as two tall half-width columns, where an iPhone in portrait stacks them.
error: User-reported: on an iPad in portrait the run screen placed the countdown and the media panel side by side as two tall half-width columns, where an iPhone in portrait stacks them.

Portrait iPad now stacks; iPhone landscape is wide AND landscape so it keeps the columns; laptops unaffected. It must be a viewport media query, not an aspect-ratio container query: `.run` is an `inline-size` container so its height cannot be queried, and the shell is pinned to the viewport so the two agree. The width-only 46rem overrides that merely widen padding were left alone.
root_cause: The two-column layout was gated on SIZE when it depends on SHAPE. `@container shell (min-width: 46rem)` was chosen so an iPhone in landscape (~52rem) gets columns, but a portrait iPad is 768-1024px = 48-64rem, so it passed the same test while having no spare height at all. Same trap as the earlier note that a portrait iPad gives the media panel a ~250x773 slot, which is why near-square illustrations rendered tiny there.

detail: User-reported with screenshots (narrow laptop window and iPhone portrait): the editor step row's buttons wrapped badly. On the phone the note button was stranded alone on a line; on both, the six-button action cluster sat hard right on a line of its own under short field lines, so no two rows agreed on where any button was. First attempt (a single `.erow__band` holding every button) made the phone WORSE — four lines instead of three — and was reverted. Second attempt (pairing the buttons plus fixing the unit select's width) was still wrong on the iPhone; the user proposed collapsing the buttons behind one button instead.
error: User-reported with screenshots (narrow laptop window and iPhone portrait): the editor step row's buttons wrapped badly. On the phone the note button was stranded alone on a line; on both, the six-button action cluster sat hard right on a line of its own under short field lines, so no two rows agreed on where any button was. First attempt (a single `.erow__band` holding every button) made the phone WORSE — four lines instead of three — and was reverted. Second attempt (pairing the buttons plus fixing the unit select's width) was still wrong on the iPhone; the user proposed collapsing the buttons behind one button instead.
fix: Two changes. (1) `.erow__own` pairs the image control with the note toggle — a pair cannot split — and stays LOOSE in the fields' wrap flow rather than being gathered into a band, so it rides along with the timing fields where the room is. `.erow__actions` keeps its bare `margin-left: auto`, which holds the right-hand column on whichever line it lands. (2) `.efield--unit` is sized by the label it SHOWS, via `data-unit` on the select and three widths in `em` (5.5 / 9 / 10.5, in em so they track the type scale). That reclaimed ~50pt — real headroom rather than a 7pt pixel race. Result: one line when wide, fields + (image, note, cluster) on a narrow window, and role/name + timing/image/note + cluster on a phone. Neither was enough — the row wants ~380pt of buttons against a phone's ~313pt, a 70pt gap no arrangement closes. Final fix: `.erow__tools` holds all eight buttons and has two jobs chosen by CSS alone — under `@container (min-width: 64rem)` it is an absolutely-positioned panel off the row's bottom-right, hidden behind a new `.erow__more` (⋯) trigger; at 64rem and over it is laid out inline at the trailing edge and the trigger is `display: none`. No width is measured in JS, so nothing needs correcting on a resize. `[data-open]` is repeated inside the container query because it beats the bare class on specificity. The panel is `position: absolute` against `.erow` (which takes `z-index` while open) rather than viewport-fixed like `Menu`, so it travels with its row on a scroll; it closes on any click inside it, since every button in it is a deed. Escape and press-outside come from the new shared `ui/useDismiss.ts`, also adopted by `Menu`.
root_cause: The image control, the note toggle and `.erow__actions` were three independent items in `.erow__main`'s `flex-wrap` flow, so wrap position was decided per item and the two 42px buttons split, stranding the note button. The deeper cause of the cramping was the unit select: a native `<select>` takes the width of its WIDEST option, so a step showing 's' held the width of 'rung each side' — about 140pt of a phone's ~311pt row, nearly all empty. That left the row ~7pt short of fitting [secs][unit][image][note] on one line. The first fix, gathering all eight buttons into one wrapping `.erow__band`, failed because flexbox places items by MAX-CONTENT width and only then shrinks them: the band measured ~380pt, so it could never share the 311pt line whatever it would have done once wrapped. It took a line of its own and split inside it — four lines where there had been three.

detail: User-reported: pressing outside the editor row's ⋯ controls panel did not close it. Introduced in the same session as the panel itself.
error: User-reported: pressing outside the editor row's ⋯ controls panel did not close it. Introduced in the same session as the panel itself.
fix: Scoped the predicate to the panel and its trigger: `panel.current?.contains(target) || more.current?.contains(target)`. The trigger must stay inside — otherwise pointerdown closes the panel and the click that follows toggles it straight back open, so it never appears to close. The row ref is gone; `.erow[data-tools]` still carries the z-index lift.
root_cause: `useDismiss`'s `inside` predicate was `row.current?.contains(target)` — the whole `<li>`. So every press within the step's own row counted as inside, including its name field, its role select and its padding, leaving the panel hanging open over the row below. Only a press in a DIFFERENT row or outside the list closed it.

detail: User-reported: the editor row's ⋯ controls panel always opened downward, so on the last rows of the list it was clipped by the scrolling container. Also reported: it opened under the whole ROW rather than under the button. Then, after the re-anchor, the panel rendered as a single vertical column of buttons instead of two horizontal rows.
error: User-reported: the editor row's ⋯ controls panel always opened downward, so on the last rows of the list it was clipped by the scrolling container. Also reported: it opened under the whole ROW rather than under the button. Then, after the re-anchor, the panel rendered as a single vertical column of buttons instead of two horizontal rows.
fix: A `useLayoutEffect` keyed on the open flag measures the row's box against `.editor__scroll`'s visible box and the panel's own `offsetHeight`, then sets `data-up`, which swaps `top` for `bottom: calc(100% + var(--step-1))`. useLayoutEffect rather than useEffect so the flip is applied in the frame the panel first paints — a plain effect renders it in the wrong place and jumps. It flips only when that helps (`below < needed && above > below`): with too little room on either side, downward can at least be scrolled into view, and a first row will not flip up into the scroller's top edge. The 4px in the measurement is `--step-1` in the CSS; the two have to agree. Then re-anchored: `.erow__menu` wraps the panel and the ⋯ button and is `position: relative`, so with the button as its only in-flow child on a narrow screen the wrapper's box IS the button's box and the panel opens directly under (or over) it. Anchoring to the row put it below both lines of a phone row, and below the note fields as well when those were open. The flip measurement moved to the button's rect for the same reason. The wrapper carries the trailing-edge auto margin in both modes, so `.erow__tools` no longer needs one. The cluster is also allowed to wrap inside the panel (never in the row) with a `100vw`-based cap, for a phone too narrow for six buttons in a line — undone again above the breakpoint in case a row was opened while narrow and then widened. That vertical collapse was caused by the re-anchor plus the wrap: an absolutely positioned box with `width: auto` is shrink-to-fit sized against its CONTAINING BLOCK, which was now the 42px `.erow__menu`, so shrink-to-fit fell back to min-content — and the wrap had made min-content one button wide. Fixed with `width: max-content` on the panel (independent of what it is anchored to) and by dropping the cluster's wrap, along with the wide-mode rule that undid it. The panel is 288px against a phone's ~361px of list, so the wrap was never needed.
root_cause: `.erow__tools` was pinned to `top: calc(100% + var(--step-1))` with no notion of available space. CSS has no way to ask; the feature that would (anchor positioning with position-try) is the same one this project already rejected as undependable, which is why Menu.tsx is hand-rolled.

detail: User-reported on iPhone in a Safari TAB: the editor's add-button footer fell partly below the bottom of the screen; after showing and dismissing the keyboard the footer became fully visible but the fixed header went off the top, with no way to scroll back and exit the editor.
error: User-reported on iPhone in a Safari TAB: the editor's add-button footer fell partly below the bottom of the screen; after showing and dismissing the keyboard the footer became fully visible but the fixed header went off the top, with no way to scroll back and exit the editor.
fix: `height: 100svh`. The small viewport is the screen with the browser UI showing, so the shell always fits what can be seen and there is no overflow to be left scrolled in; and since nothing here scrolls, the browser UI never retracts to leave a gap. svh and lvh are both STABLE — neither responds to the keyboard — so the original dvh problem stays fixed. On a home-screen install there is no browser UI, so svh == lvh == dvh and the install is unchanged. `.modal` keeps `100dvh` deliberately: a dialog should track the keyboard.
root_cause: `html, body, #root { height: 100lvh }`. The LARGE viewport is the screen with the browser UI RETRACTED, so in a tab with Safari's address bar and toolbar showing the shell was taller than the visible screen by their height. Both symptoms follow from that: the bottom band of each screen sat under the toolbar, and content taller than the viewport is scrollable OVERFLOW which `overflow: hidden` only clips, not prevents — so the keyboard's focus-reveal scrolled the document and left it scrolled, and `hidden` meant the user could not scroll back what the browser had scrolled. `lvh` had been chosen over `dvh` to stop the keyboard reflowing the app, which was correct but overshot: it fixed the keyboard by picking the TALLEST stable viewport when the SHORTEST was the one that always fits.

detail: Pasted 25 Aug email: 28 lines reported as skipped, and five 30/30 exercises silently replaced by five steps named "WORK"
error: Pasted 25 Aug email: 28 lines reported as skipped, and five 30/30 exercises silently replaced by five steps named "WORK"
fix: Added the idea a directive can license the line below it (expectItem/pendingMs), so "30 sec WORK", "Minute 4", "LAST 20 SECONDS" and "Every time you finish a round:" name the step on the next bare line. EMOM minutes compile to 60s steps carrying their rep target, with the balance returned as rest when the step states a shorter time. ROUNDS accepts "Repeat" and "×" and wraps the loose steps above it when read below them (guarded to plain lists so a ladder is never swallowed). The 25 Aug email arrived on a second one whose forms name no exercise on the line that times them ("30 sec WORK" then the exercise below), state the round count AFTER the block ("Repeat 2 rounds"), and use EMOM/AMRAP block headings.
