detail: Media panel fallback text set at the 1rem floor, using three lines of an eleven-line box
error: Media panel fallback text set at the 1rem floor, using three lines of an eleven-line box
fix: Added `fitPanel(text)` returning `{fit, lines}` from one calculation. Solving `total*s^2*FIT_ADVANCE/FIT_BUDGET <= FIT_HEIGHT_BUDGET` gives `s = sqrt(FIT_HEIGHT_BUDGET*FIT_BUDGET/(FIT_ADVANCE*total))`, still floored by the longest-word bound from `fitCqi`, with `lines` the count at that size so the CSS height term agrees rather than shrinking again. `--fit` 12.96/`--lines` 43 became 6.79/11, roughly 16px to 42px on a 650px panel. Reproduces `wordCount` exactly for short names, which is asserted. `wordCount` removed: `RunScreen`'s MediaPanel was its only caller.
root_cause: `.panel__empty` sizes with `min(--fit * 1cqi, 72cqh / --lines)`, and `--lines` came from `wordCount`, an upper bound justified by `fitCqi` sizing so the LONGEST word fits a line, so each word may take one. Sound for a two or three word exercise name, wildly pessimistic for a paragraph: a 43-word AMRAP round asked for 43 lines, so the height term was 1.67cqh, the size clamped to the 1rem floor, and at that size the text wrapped into three lines. The real error is that the line count is not independent of the size it divides: shrinking text cuts the line count as well as the line height.

detail: iPhone Safari: the section heading drew over the header and the step count drew over the step name
error: iPhone Safari: the section heading drew over the header and the step count drew over the step name
fix: Moved the heading out of the count column into `.run__heading` in the header, under the routine name. That row is `auto`, so it takes the height it needs and the body's `1fr` gives way: no budget to re-tune, and the count column is byte-identical to before. It also removed a duplication, since the list layout had its own `<h2>` for the same thing, so the section is now named once for both layouts. Clamped to two lines with `-webkit-line-clamp` so a long name cannot grow the header and take the space from the countdown it captions. A test asserts the heading appears exactly once, inside the `header`, and never inside `.count__lead`.
root_cause: The section heading was added to `.count__lead`, whose column budget is documented in the `--clock-max` comment as meta 20 + label 12 + name 14 + clock 52 = 98cqh, leaving about 2cqh of slack. A long section name ("FULL-LEG BURN – EVERY MINUTE ON THE MINUTE") wrapped to two lines on the narrowest phone, the lead outgrew its `minmax(0, 1fr)` row, and because it is `align-content: center` the overflow spilled BOTH ways: up onto the header and down onto the meta row. The `.count` comment already recorded this exact failure from a previous occasion, which is what named the cause.

detail: The Send menu on a library row opened far below its button ("miles below")
error: The Send menu on a library row opened far below its button ("miles below")
fix: Render the list through `createPortal` into `document.body`, so `position: fixed` resolves against the viewport wherever the trigger happens to live. Pinned by a test that mounts a Menu inside a transformed ancestor and asserts the list's parent is `document.body`. Placement was separately rewritten to measure the real box rather than assume 208px, to flip above the trigger when there is no room below, and to right-align when a left-aligned list would overrun the screen.
root_cause: `.menu__list` is `position: fixed` and placed from the trigger's `getBoundingClientRect()`, which is correct ONLY while no ancestor establishes a containing block for fixed descendants. `.library__scroll` carries `transform: translateY(calc(var(--pull, 0) * 1px))` for pull-to-refresh, applied unconditionally, and even `translateY(0)` is enough to make that element the containing block. The list was therefore positioned against the scrolled list's border box rather than the viewport, so the further down the library was scrolled the further off it landed. The header menus (Routines, Sort) never showed it because they sit OUTSIDE the scroller, which is why the bug only appeared once a Menu was put inside a row.

detail: The help tray's contents would not scroll; long help ran off the bottom of the screen
error: The help tray's contents would not scroll; long help ran off the bottom of the screen
fix: `height: 100dvh` on `.tray`, which is exactly what `.modal` already does and how the cause was found: the two dialogs differed in one property and only one of them scrolled. `dvh` rather than `svh` matches `.modal`, since a dialog wants to reflow for the keyboard and is not the thing being scrolled.
root_cause: The UA stylesheet gives every `<dialog>` `height: fit-content`, and `.tray` never overrode it. That beats the `inset: 0 0 0 auto` above it: with `top` and `bottom` both 0 the height would otherwise resolve to the viewport, but an explicit `height` wins and the box is over-constrained, so `bottom: 0` is dropped. The tray therefore grew to its CONTENT height rather than capping at the screen, which left `.tray__body`'s `minmax(0, 1fr)` grid row with no definite height to scroll inside. Everything else was already right: the grid rows, `min-height: 0`, `overflow-y: auto`. It only showed once enough help bullets were added for the content to exceed one screen, which happened on 2026-08-27 when the generator's help was written.

detail: The generator's sections shape ignored "what to work": asking for Core alone still built Arms & Shoulders and Legs sections
error: The generator's sections shape ignored "what to work": asking for Core alone still built Arms & Shoulders and Legs sections
fix: Narrow each theme's areas to `spec.areas` and drop a theme left with nothing, noting how many were dropped. The WARM-UP is exempt, for the same reason it ignores the equipment filter: you warm the whole of yourself up whatever the session then works. Found by Wayne asking whether both shapes honoured the selection rather than by a test.
root_cause: `SECTION_THEMES` carries its own `areas` per theme, harvested from the corpus, and `sectionsRoutine` took them as written. The user's `spec.areas` was never intersected with them, so every theme built regardless of what had been asked for. The circuit shape had always intersected, which is why the bug was invisible on the shape most used: the two shapes were written weeks apart and only one of them read the answer.

detail: A step whose weight was cleared showed the placeholder '65kg, red band' in the editor instead of the weights-page value, and no weight at all on the run screen.
error: A step whose weight was cleared showed the placeholder '65kg, red band' in the editor instead of the weights-page value, and no weight at all on the run screen.
fix: Added findLoad() in loads.ts: exact key first, then a word-by-word match where a shorter word may be the start of a longer one ('ab' finds 'abdominal'). The word COUNT and order must match, which keeps 'Incline Chest Press' away from 'Incline Cable Converging Chest Press'; 'abductor' and 'adductor' still do not match since neither starts the other; two candidates return nothing rather than guessing; a one-letter word never matches. weightFor(), fillLoads() and stripLoads() all go through it, so the editor hint and the run screen can no longer disagree. Probed against all 67 loadable exercises for collisions: none.
root_cause: The lookup key was an exact folded name. Routine 2 names the step '12 x Seated Ab Crunch'; the exercise table takes its names from the manufacturer's guide and calls it 'Seated Abdominal Crunch'. foldName gives 'seated ab crunch' against 'seated abdominal crunch', so neither the editor hint nor fillLoads found anything. Affected every exercise a routine writes in shorthand, not just this one.

detail: A generated sections routine started straight on the warm-up; a pasted routine opens on five seconds to get ready.
error: A generated sections routine started straight on the warm-up; a pasted routine opens on five seconds to get ready.
fix: generateRoutine's sections branch prepends segment({name:'Get ready', role:'prepare', durationMs: GET_READY_MS}) imported from pasteFormat.ts, so it matches the parser exactly and writeRoutine strips it on Send as text. GenerateDialog counts blocks of kind 'section' instead of all blocks. Tests use sectionsOf() to skip the get-ready; README paragraph added.
root_cause: sectionsRoutine() returned the sections only and generateRoutine() used them as the block list. The parser's getReady() prepends a loose 5s prepare step; the generator never did.

detail: No whistle at Start, and no cue when a gate opened: the @0 opening cue of every run was never scheduled.
error: No whistle at Start, and no cue when a gate opened: the @0 opening cue of every run was never scheduled.
fix: dueCues looks back by CANCEL_GRACE_MS; engine.scheduleTone drops a cue only when it is later than the same grace (was a literal 50ms). Test mounts the hook with elapsed=3 and expects the whistle.
root_cause: dueCues opened its window AT the elapsed time (cuesBetween keeps atMs >= fromMs). readElapsed is performance.now() based and the effect runs after React commits, so the first arm always saw a small positive elapsed and the cue at 0 fell outside the window. The existing hook test passed only because its readElapsed returned exactly 0.

detail: The opening cue of the second and later runs was silent even when run 0's played.
error: The opening cue of the second and later runs was silent even when run 0's played.
fix: The hook remembers which allCues the set describes and clears it when the run's cues change identity. Test rerenders runIndex 0 -> 1 -> 2 on a work/gate/rest routine and expects a cue at zero each time.
root_cause: The dedup Set of queued cue keys (kind@atMs, run-relative) was only cleared when not running or muted, and requeueable never forgets a cue at @0, so run 0's 'work-start@0' key suppressed the identical key in every later run.

detail: A failed save, delete, copy or favourite went unreported; the editor returned to the library as if it had saved.
error: A failed save, delete, copy or favourite went unreported; the editor returned to the library as if it had saved.
fix: useLibrary wraps every mutation in guarded(): failure sets `error` (shown by the library screen) and rethrows with the same words; success clears it. App.onSave awaits add() before leaving the editor; EditorScreen catches a rejected onSave and shows a notice keeping the draft.
root_cause: Every mutation was fired with `void library.x()` and useLibrary only set `error` during the initial load, so a rejected IndexedDB write was an unhandled rejection.

detail: One unreadable IndexedDB record errored the whole library and could not be deleted.
error: One unreadable IndexedDB record errored the whole library and could not be deleted.
fix: readWorkouts() checks and migrates one record at a time, skips and counts the unreadable ones, leaves them in the store; useLibrary shows the count in `error`. listWorkouts() returns the readable ones. Test with two corrupt rows.
root_cause: listWorkouts mapped migrateWorkout over every record; a record with no `blocks` or a group with no `children` threw, the list failed with workouts=[], and remove() needs the list.

detail: Starring a routine re-stamped updatedAt and jumped it to the top of the recent sort.
error: Starring a routine re-stamped updatedAt and jumped it to the top of the recent sort.
fix: toggleFavourite spreads the flag without stamp() and lost its `now` parameter. Test asserts updatedAt unchanged.
root_cause: toggleFavourite went through stamp(), which sets updatedAt, although putWorkout's contract says metadata-only writes must not.

detail: A synchronous throw from indexedDB.open was cached as a permanently rejected promise.
error: A synchronous throw from indexedDB.open was cached as a permanently rejected promise.
fix: openDb assigns the promise then attaches promise.catch(forget), so any rejection un-caches itself after assignment. Test scripts a 'throw' open followed by a good one.
root_cause: `opening ??= new Promise(executor)`: the executor runs before the assignment, so a forget() inside it (or in onerror) could only work for asynchronous failures; a sync throw rejected a promise that was then assigned and never cleared.

detail: Share links imported unchecked workout metadata, block ids were optional, and dropped photos were not reported.
error: Share links imported unchecked workout metadata, block ids were optional, and dropped photos were not reported.
fix: decodeRoutine runs isWorkout (now exported from bundle.ts) and builds from named fields; isBlock requires a string id; isSegment/isWorkout check role and colour against their unions; LibraryScreen.share() reports uploaded photos a link cannot carry. sortWorkouts by duration now uses timed + estimated length precomputed once; duplicate() reads names from the store.
root_cause: decodeRoutine validated blocks only and spread `...workout` into the store; isBlock accepted a missing id although gates key on it; encodeRoutine discarded shareable()'s droppedImages count.

detail: Two consecutive drags in the editor were one undo step; a cancelled drag left an undo step that did nothing.
error: Two consecutive drags in the editor were one undo step; a cancelled drag left an undo step that did nothing.
fix: history.ts gained endRun() (typing -> null) and discardRun() (drop the run, restore the state before it, nothing to redo). onEnd calls endRun, onCancel calls discardRun. Tests: two drags are two undo steps; Escape leaves Undo disabled.
root_cause: Every drag frame pushed with the coalescing key 'drag' and onEnd never reset history.typing, so the next drag's first move coalesced into the previous drag. onCancel pushed the original tree under the same key, coalescing into the run and leaving present === past top.

detail: Cmd/Ctrl+Z while typing an uncommitted note deleted the step being typed in (undid the previous document edit).
error: Cmd/Ctrl+Z while typing an uncommitted note deleted the step being typed in (undid the previous document edit).
fix: The handler returns without acting when document.activeElement is an input whose value differs from its defaultValue (the routine name is controlled and exempt). Test types in a note, presses Cmd+Z, and expects the earlier rename to survive.
root_cause: The global keydown handler preventDefaulted native undo for every field, but note/alternative/weight are uncontrolled inputs committed on blur, so their keystrokes were not in the history yet.

detail: Focusing a section's instruction field zoomed the page on iPhone.
error: Focusing a section's instruction field zoomed the page on iPhone.
fix: Floor raised to 1rem with the reason in a comment.
root_cause: .efield--note floored its font-size at 0.9rem (14.4px); iOS Safari zooms any focused input under 16px. Every other .efield floors at 1rem for this reason.

detail: A .tabata step imported with role 'custom' showed 'Get ready' in the type select; a Recover step toggled to timed got 20s instead of 60s.
error: A .tabata step imported with role 'custom' showed 'Get ready' in the type select; a Recover step toggled to timed got 20s instead of 60s.
fix: The select offers a Custom option only when the step already has that role, so the add bar gains no button. retarget uses DEFAULT_SECONDS (now exported from blocks.ts).
root_cause: ROLES omitted 'custom' (a legal SegmentRole the importer emits), so <select value='custom'> had no matching option. retarget used a literal 20_000 instead of DEFAULT_SECONDS[role].

detail: A reps group outside a list section showed only its first step; one tap skipped the rest unseen.
error: A reps group outside a list section showed only its first step; one tap skipped the rest unseen.
fix: gateKey() returns null unless the nearest section on the path is display 'list', so a group anywhere else advances a step at a time. Test compiles a top-level reps group and a timer-section group to one run per step; three shape tests gained list sections; engine README and types.ts comments reworded.
root_cause: gateKey() collapsed every self-paced step of any group into one gate, but listMode() only draws the list inside a display:'list' section; everywhere else the countdown view renders the gate's first entry only.

detail: A routine over 10,000 steps white-screened the app on Start.
error: A routine over 10,000 steps white-screened the app on Start.
fix: isWorkout() rejects a routine whose stepCount exceeds MAX_TIMELINE_ENTRIES (bundles and share links); the editor disables Save over the limit and says so beside the count; App wraps the screens in a new ErrorBoundary whose Back remounts them on the library.
root_cause: compile() throws TimelineTooLargeError inside useMemo during render; nothing caught it and there was no error boundary. The editor capped times at 99 per level but not nesting, and bundle/share-link validation checked shape, not size.

detail: Tidy exercise names dropped side qualifiers and trailing counts: 'side plank left' -> 'Side Plank', 'Quad stretch × 3 (left & right)' lost the × 3.
error: Tidy exercise names dropped side qualifiers and trailing counts: 'side plank left' -> 'Side Plank', 'Quad stretch × 3 (left & right)' lost the × 3.
fix: split() also peels TRAILING_SIDE and TRAILING_COUNT, TRAILING_DASH allows no space before the dash, and canonicalName refuses a core that still holds a side word or a digit. Tests cover each form and the refusal.
root_cause: split() peeled only a trailing load, parenthesis or spaced dash into `trail`; foldName() throws left/right/per leg/counts away to match, and the canonical name replaced the whole core without them. TRAILING_DASH also required a space before the dash, so 'squat– 5 each side' was not peeled.

detail: Text export corrupted a step whose note contained 'for N seconds' or a parenthesis: 'Plank (hold for 2 seconds…) - 40 seconds' read back as a 2-second step called 'Plank (hold', with `lost` empty.
error: Text export corrupted a step whose note contained 'for N seconds' or a parenthesis: 'Plank (hold for 2 seconds…) - 40 seconds' read back as a 2-second step called 'Plank (hold', with `lost` empty.
fix: stepLines re-parses each line it writes (bullet stripped) and compares name, duration and count; a mismatch drops the note and reports it, and a line still wrong is reported. Two round-trip tests.
root_cause: The grammar has no escaping; FOR_DURATION is tried before TRAILING_DURATION in parseItem and TRAILING_PAREN is [^()]*, so the note's text was read as the step's timing or name. The writer never checked what it emitted.

detail: A heading with nothing under it at the end of the text vanished with no `skipped` entry ('Cool down walk for 2 minutes' as the last line).
error: A heading with nothing under it at the end of the text vanished with no `skipped` entry ('Cool down walk for 2 minutes' as the last line).
fix: The parser records the line that opened a section and the count of lines read under it; a section closed at the END of the text with no children and no lines under it is pushed to `skipped`. Mid-text empty headings (a title split over two lines, or lines already refused) stay silent. The corpus test now records the one line this surfaces in 2026-07-13-trampoline, a closing 'Challenge' heading that was being dropped.
root_cause: closeSection() discarded a childless section silently. NAMED_SECTION matches 'cool down…' so the line opened a section that closed empty at end of input.

detail: The timeline was recompiled and the tick and cue effects re-armed a few milliseconds into every run.
error: The timeline was recompiled and the tick and cue effects re-armed a few milliseconds into every run.
fix: useMemo keyed on view; RunScreen receives the memoised routine.
root_cause: withWeights(view.workout, currentWeights()) was called inline in JSX, returning a new object per render whenever any load fills; markRun resolving after Start re-rendered App.

detail: A paused cue within the cancel grace played during the pause and again after resume.
error: A paused cue within the cancel grace played during the pause and again after resume.
fix: Paused (or muted while running) prunes with requeueable; idle/complete still clears so a restart gets its whistle. Test pauses at 24.9s and expects no second bell at 25s.
root_cause: The not-running branch cleared the dedup set wholesale while cancelPending spared cues within CANCEL_GRACE_MS.

detail: Holding an arrow key on the run screen skipped a step every ~30ms; hardware Back or closing the tab left a run with no confirmation.
error: Holding an arrow key on the run screen skipped a step every ~30ms; hardware Back or closing the tab left a run with no confirmation.
fix: event.repeat returns early; a beforeunload handler is registered while inProgress.
root_cause: No event.repeat guard; no beforeunload while a run was in progress (only the editor had one).

detail: describeRoutine named a three-section routine '5 sections'; the dialog hard-coded 3.
error: describeRoutine named a three-section routine '5 sections'; the dialog hard-coded 3.
fix: SECTIONS_FEWEST is exported and used by all three. Test names sections:3 as '3 sections'.
root_cause: sectionsRoutine clamped at SECTIONS_FEWEST (3) while describeRoutine used SECTIONS_MIN (5) and GenerateDialog used a literal 3.

detail: A date line such as 2026-04-16 parsed as a rep ladder and claimed the next step as its main lift.
error: A date line such as 2026-04-16 parsed as a rep ladder and claimed the next step as its main lift.
fix: Rungs are at most two digits (corpus max is 20). Test: the date is reported in skipped and no ladder is built.
root_cause: LADDER matched any three dash-separated numbers of any length.

detail: Landscape iPhone: the Next slab and the wide-layout run body ignored the safe-area insets; a wake-lock release event could orphan a newer lock; scripts/*.ts were typechecked by nothing.
error: Landscape iPhone: the Next slab and the wide-layout run body ignored the safe-area insets; a wake-lock release event could orphan a newer lock; scripts/*.ts were typechecked by nothing.
fix: Both paddings add the insets; the release listener checks sentinel.current === lock; tsconfig.scripts.json (extends app config, includes scripts, vitest.harvest.config.ts and src) is referenced from tsconfig.json.
root_cause: .run__sheet and the landscape .run__body padded without --safe-left/right; useWakeLock nulled the shared sentinel on any release; tsconfig.node included only vite.config.ts.

detail: A '4 Rounds' line after a 10-minute AMRAP wrapped the AMRAP clock in the repeat (40 minutes); 'Then:' under an AMRAP added what followed to its round.
error: A '4 Rounds' line after a 10-minute AMRAP wrapped the AMRAP clock in the repeat (40 minutes); 'Then:' under an AMRAP added what followed to its round.
fix: The ROUNDS branch records whether an AMRAP was open before flushing and skips the trailing wrap if so; THEN flushes the AMRAP. Tests for both.
root_cause: flushAmrap() ran before the trailing-repeat check, so the AMRAP segment counted as a loose step to swallow; the THEN branch never called flushAmrap().

detail: A bulleted duration ladder ('- Plank 20sec-30sec-40sec') read as one 20s step; a bare 'Rest 30 seconds' in a section became a note; a joined pair under a 'Minute N' heading split into two steps.
error: A bulleted duration ladder ('- Plank 20sec-30sec-40sec') read as one 20s step; a bare 'Rest 30 seconds' in a section became a note; a joined pair under a 'Minute N' heading split into two steps.
fix: readDurationLadder() is shared by the line and bullet paths; a 'rest N sec/min' line without between/after/each is a rest step; a bullet under pendingFill goes through addMinute. Tests for each.
root_cause: DURATION_LADDER ran on the raw line only, never on the bullet's text; SECTION_NOTE's rest\b matched before the loose-step fallback; the bullet path split JOINED_ITEMS without checking pendingFill.

detail: 'Arnold Press' and 'Arnold Presses' folded to different keys ('arnold pres' / 'arnold press'), so the prescription table held both and ALIASES needed 'chest pres'.
error: 'Arnold Press' and 'Arnold Presses' folded to different keys ('arnold pres' / 'arnold press'), so the prescription table held both and ALIASES needed 'chest pres'.
fix: foldName keeps a trailing 'ss'; the harvest was re-run (prescription.ts re-keyed, duplicate rows merged); ALIASES key updated; test added.
root_cause: The trailing-s strip did not exempt words ending in a double s.

detail: A generated sections routine's estimatedTotalMs was short by rungs x accessory time; only 6 of 19 ladder shapes were ever drawn; Torso Rotations and Inchworms could never be generated.
error: A generated sections routine's estimatedTotalMs was short by rungs x accessory time; only 6 of 19 ladder shapes were ever drawn; Torso Rotations and Inchworms could never be generated.
fix: compile.ts exports blocksDurationMs and generate.ts uses it; weightedPick over all ladders by `seen`; the warm-up draws from every area. Tests: >6 distinct shapes over 60 seeds; a torso mobility move appears.
root_cause: A local totalMs counted a ladder's children once; LADDER_COUNTS was indexed with Math.min(6, length); the warm-up drew from ['lower','upper'] only.

detail: Two steps sharing an uploaded photo: the second resolved to null for good when both were resolved in one render.
error: Two steps sharing an uploaded photo: the second resolved to null for good when both were resolved in one render.
fix: The cache is a Map of in-flight reads; a second caller awaits the first. Test resolves the same ref twice concurrently.
root_cause: The negative cache (a Set of hashes) was written before the read resolved, so a concurrent caller skipped the read and found no object URL.

detail: putBlob announced a stored blob before the write committed; a commit-time abort left resolveMedia believing in bytes never written.
error: putBlob announced a stored blob before the write committed; a commit-time abort left resolveMedia believing in bytes never written.
fix: A readwrite resolves on transaction.oncomplete; a readonly still resolves on success. The test fake completes the transaction a tick after the request.
root_cause: run() resolved on request.onsuccess for every mode.

detail: Hardware/browser Back left a run or an unsaved edit with no confirmation.
error: Hardware/browser Back left a run or an unsaved edit with no confirmation.
fix: App pushes one history entry while a screen other than the library is open and pops it on return; popstate on run/edit re-pushes and bumps a backRequest prop that RunScreen and EditorScreen answer with their own exit handlers; other screens go to the library.
root_cause: The app had no history entries; Back left the page (beforeunload covered only the tab-close case).

detail: USER REPORTED: countdown numerals small for a step of minutes ('1:30' sized for the whole step).
error: USER REPORTED: countdown numerals small for a step of minutes ('1:30' sized for the whole step).
fix: Measured from timer.secondsLeft: the width class changes only where a character is lost (10:00 to 9:59, 1:00 to 59), the minute marks; clockWidth's floor of 2 keeps 10 to 9 steady.
root_cause: clockChars was measured once from the step's starting text so the size never changed mid-step.

detail: Editor lows: no Ctrl+Y redo; focus fell to the body after Delete/Add/Duplicate; a cleared group label or section note was stored as ''; Menu items keyed by label with aria-checked on menuitem.
error: Editor lows: no Ctrl+Y redo; focus fell to the body after Delete/Add/Duplicate; a cleared group label or section note was stored as ''; Menu items keyed by label with aria-checked on menuitem.
fix: Ctrl+Y redoes; focusAfter names a row index and selector applied after render; patched() deletes keys set to ''; Menu keys by index+label and uses menuitemradio when selectable. Tests for focus and empty-field removal.
root_cause: Redo only on Shift+Z; the pressed button unmounted with its row; updateRepeat/Ladder/Section spread the patch without deleting empties; Menu used label keys and a plain menuitem role for choosable items.

detail: Library lows: drop overlay flickered crossing children; done rows on the run sheet fell under 4.5:1 on the phase wash.
error: Library lows: drop overlay flickered crossing children; done rows on the run sheet fell under 4.5:1 on the phase wash.
fix: Enter/leave counter drives the overlay; done rows use --bone-dim (the strike-through carries the state).
root_cause: dragleave fires entering a child; --bone-faint over the gradient top measured ~3.6:1.

detail: Storage/media lows: a large backup download could be cancelled by an early object-URL revoke; an all-rejected bundle threw and lost the names; two tabs kept stale weights/paces caches; pull-to-refresh 'busy' never reset; a huge data URL was decoded before the size cap; AudioContext construction and resume() were unguarded.
error: Storage/media lows: a large backup download could be cancelled by an early object-URL revoke; an all-rejected bundle threw and lost the names; two tabs kept stale weights/paces caches; pull-to-refresh 'busy' never reset; a huge data URL was decoded before the size cap; AudioContext construction and resume() were unguarded.
fix: Revoke after 60s; fromBundle returns {workouts: [], rejected} unless the file had no routines at all; weights.ts/paces.ts drop their cache on a storage event; finally resets busy; encoded length checked first; AudioContext guarded and resume().catch(). Bundle tests updated to expect the names.
root_cause: Revoke on the next macrotask; fromBundle threw when no routine was readable even with rejected names collected; no storage-event listener; no finally on the refresh promise; cap checked after atob; ctx.resume() unhandled and new AudioContext() outside try.

detail: Routines lows: shouted REST read as a heading; '0 Rounds' built an empty group; '10 xtreme pushups' lost its x; a pyramid row naming an undefined rung was shortened silently; unknown warm-up/cool-down exercises fell back silently; sections with no areas built a warm-up-only routine and sections:NaN threw a misleading error; group/ladder labels other than Set were dropped from text export without a word; the two-pass fuzzy matcher was duplicated in rename.ts and loads.ts.
error: Routines lows: shouted REST read as a heading; '0 Rounds' built an empty group; '10 xtreme pushups' lost its x; a pyramid row naming an undefined rung was shortened silently; unknown warm-up/cool-down exercises fell back silently; sections with no areas built a warm-up-only routine and sections:NaN threw a misleading error; group/ladder labels other than Set were dropped from text export without a word; the two-pass fuzzy matcher was duplicated in rename.ts and loads.ts.
fix: SHOUTED_SECTION excludes rest/work and needs a 3-letter word; 0 rounds is reported in skipped; LEADING_COUNT requires whitespace after x; undefined rungs report the row; named() notes the fallback; areas:[] throws the dialog's message and NaN falls to the typical count; labels other than Set/Round are reported in lost; closestKey() in foldName.ts is shared. Tests for each.
root_cause: See each: SHOUTED_SECTION had no word list; ROUNDS accepted 0; LEADING_COUNT's [×x]\s* ate a leading x; expandPyramid filtered undefined rungs quietly; named() had no note; sectionsRoutine did not validate areas or sections; repeatLines/ladderLines ignored labels; findLoad and match() each carried the matcher.

detail: USER REPORTED: in the editor a ladder row was labelled 'Set' and a sets row 'Round'; the run screen read 'Set 3 of 9' over a ladder.
error: USER REPORTED: in the editor a ladder row was labelled 'Set' and a sets row 'Round'; the run screen read 'Set 3 of 9' over a ladder.
fix: Ladders default to 'Rung' (editor, generator, compile fallback, run captions) and migrate.ts relabels a stored 'Set'/'Round' ladder to 'Rung', leaving a typed name alone; the generator emits 'Set'; App migrates every draft on its way into the editor; each group row shows a kind badge (Sets / Ladder / Section) in the group's colour.
root_cause: newLadder, the generator and compile's fallback all gave ladders the label 'Set'; the generator's sections shape and the parser emit 'Round' for repeat groups, and a generated or pasted draft went into the editor without the migration that turns 'Round' into 'Set' on read. The group rows had no text but the free-text label field, so the kind was invisible.

detail: USER REPORTED: the generator did not choose from the full set of exercises. 22 of 147 were never drawn: every lower-body cardio and mobility move, the trampoline moves included.
error: USER REPORTED: the generator did not choose from the full set of exercises. 22 of 147 were never drawn: every lower-body cardio and mobility move, the trampoline moves included.
fix: draw() takes one exercise from each area in turn until the quota is met. Probe after the fix: every catalogue exercise is drawn within 600 section routines. Test: over 40 seeds the warm-up includes a lower-body cardio or mobility move.
root_cause: sectionsRoutine's draw() walked the areas in order and stopped at the quota, so 'four mobility, four cardio' for the warm-up filled from upper and torso before lower was reached.

detail: USER REPORTED (assessment): generated sections routines put the ladders on General Body and Core and rounds on Legs and Finisher; the instructor writes the Finisher as a ladder in 14/16 and Core as rounds in every routine since July.
error: USER REPORTED (assessment): generated sections routines put the ladders on General Body and Core and rounds on Legs and Finisher; the instructor writes the Finisher as a ladder in 14/16 and Core as rounds in every routine since July.
fix: THEME_SHAPE maps each theme to its corpus shape (climb / rounds / ladder / coreRounds / finisher); mains drawn preferring rung-capable lifts; holds excluded from counted draws; Core and Finisher get their loose tails; warm-up is cardio-then-mobility from WARM_UP_MOVES. 13 new tests, including a write-then-parse round trip.

detail: USER REPORTED: the area filters looked broken in sections mode. A Core-only routine was named 'Bodyweight Core, 6 sections' while holding 4, and kept sections named 'General Body' and 'Finisher'.
error: USER REPORTED: the area filters looked broken in sections mode. A Core-only routine was named 'Bodyweight Core, 6 sections' while holding 4, and kept sections named 'General Body' and 'Finisher'.
fix: generateRoutine names a sections routine from sections.length; the dialog leaves the name to the generator and shows result.workout.name as the placeholder; themeName() renames narrowed themes (Abs, Lower Body, Upper Body & Abs, Legs Finisher, Core Finisher).
root_cause: describeRoutine was given the count ASKED, and the dialog passed that name in so the generator could not correct it; theme names ignored the area narrowing. The filter itself was correct (probed: no out-of-area strength exercise in 10 combinations).

detail: During the rewrite: 'Sit-ups with a Reach' came out as a 30-second hold, and Front Punches opened every generated warm-up.
error: During the rewrite: 'Sit-ups with a Reach' came out as a 30-second hold, and Front Punches opened every generated warm-up.

detail: ExerciseField.test.tsx: TypeError: document.getElementById(...)?.scrollIntoView is not a function — every test that opened the suggestion list found no listbox at all
error: ExerciseField.test.tsx: TypeError: document.getElementById(...)?.scrollIntoView is not a function — every test that opened the suggestion list found no listbox at all
fix: Feature-test before calling: `if (typeof row?.scrollIntoView === 'function')`. Nothing else in src/ used scrollIntoView, so there was no existing stub or setup file to follow.
root_cause: The effect that keeps the arrow-key selection in view called scrollIntoView unconditionally. jsdom ships no layout and therefore no scrollIntoView, so the effect threw; React tore the subtree down and the portalled list vanished, which read as 'the list never opens' rather than as a missing DOM method.

detail: exerciseOptions.test.ts: exerciseRows(options, 'leg') returned every exercise under kit headings instead of the two matches
error: exerciseOptions.test.ts: exerciseRows(options, 'leg') returned every exercise under kit headings instead of the two matches
fix: needleOf(): fold, and where folding leaves nothing keep the letters instead. A half-typed word is not a routine and does not need a routine's rules. Test added asserting 'leg' filters to two and produces no headings.
root_cause: The matcher folded the QUERY with foldName, which drops a trailing limb ('Fire Hydrant Left Leg' names a side). foldName('leg') is '', and an empty needle means 'nothing typed', so typing leg — or arm, or side — answered a search with all 147 exercises. Those are prefixes anyone reaches on the way to Leg Press.

detail: EditorScreen.test.tsx: Unable to find an accessible element with the role "option" and name /^Glute Kickback\b/
error: EditorScreen.test.tsx: Unable to find an accessible element with the role "option" and name /^Glute Kickback\b/
fix: An explicit aria-label on the option: `name` alone, or `${name}, ${hint}`. Controls exactly what is announced and gives the tests a stable name to match.
root_cause: An option row is a grid of three spans with no whitespace between them, so the computed accessible name ran them together: 'Glute KickbackStation 7 · each side'. A space text node between the spans would have been an anonymous fourth grid item and would have shifted the columns.

detail: USER REPORTED (screenshot): the exercise dropdown printed the name one letter per line with the hint set huge across it
error: USER REPORTED (screenshot): the exercise dropdown printed the name one letter per line with the hint set huge across it
fix: Name and hint STACKED in one column beside the picture, and every size in the list written in rem with no .label classes anywhere in it. A dropdown is dense by nature and does not want the screen's type scale.
root_cause: Two faults in one row. (1) The option was a three-column grid, thumbnail | name | hint, and the hint is white-space: nowrap, so it took the width it needed and the name's minmax(0,1fr) column collapsed to min-content: one character wide. (2) The label classes size type in cqi, and the list is PORTALLED to the body where there is no container, so the units fell back to the viewport and set a dropdown in the screen's display scale.

detail: USER REPORTED: the exercise dropdown does not scroll
error: USER REPORTED: the exercise dropdown does not scroll
fix: Ignore a scroll whose target is inside the list. Also capped the list at 384px and placed it from scrollHeight rather than the already-clamped box height, so above/below is decided from the height the list would really be.
root_cause: The close-on-scroll listener is bound on the CAPTURE phase, because a scroll event does not bubble. That means it also saw the list scrolling inside itself, so the first drag through the 147 exercises closed it. Menu.tsx has the same listener and never showed it: its lists are seven items long and never scroll.

detail: USER REPORTED: removing an image on the Exercises page left the old thumbnail in the row
error: USER REPORTED: removing an image on the Exercises page left the old thumbnail in the row
fix: The effect clears the map when nothing is pending, srcOf reads the synchronous map first, and both are guarded by `shownPictures.has(name)` so an exercise with no picture resolves to null immediately. Two tests: removal, and one picture replacing another.
root_cause: The page resolves its 147 images once, in two passes: a synchronous one for bundled paths and an effect for blobs. The effect's map only ever GREW (it returned early when nothing needed a blob), and srcOf read it FIRST, so a removed photo's URL was still there and still preferred.

detail: CI (Deploy to GitHub Pages) failed: ReferenceError: indexedDB is not defined — src/storage/db.ts:37, via ExercisesScreen's image effect. All 1161 tests passed; vitest reported '1 error' and exited 1.
error: CI (Deploy to GitHub Pages) failed: ReferenceError: indexedDB is not defined — src/storage/db.ts:37, via ExercisesScreen's image effect. All 1161 tests passed; vitest reported '1 error' and exited 1.
fix: Catch per read in the page effect and in useMediaUrl: a failed read resolves to null, so the row shows no picture, exactly as for a photo left on another device. Test added with an unreadable local ref.
root_cause: The page's image effect awaited resolveMedia with no catch. Reading a blob can THROW rather than miss: openDb throws where site data is blocked, which is a private window, a browser refusing storage, and jsdom. The new test wrote a local MediaRef, so the effect took that path for the first time. useMediaUrl had the same unguarded pattern.

detail: Pressing M while a picture opened from Preview was on screen muted the app from behind the dialog.

detail: ExercisesScreen.test.tsx: TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an accessible element with the role "button" and name "Change Sandbag Lunge"

detail: USER-INVISIBLE UNTIL SHARED: writeRoutine dropped the rep count from every step that is also timed, so an EMOM section exported as text lost all its targets

fix: emomLines(): a repeat whose children are all 60s work segments, at least one stating a fixed count, is written as '6-Minute EMOM' / 'N Rounds' / 'Minute 1: 12 x Bicep Curls'. root_cause: stepLines writes one bulleted line per step, and a trailing duration ends the name there: '12 x Bicep Curls - 60 seconds' reads back as a step CALLED '12 x Bicep Curls'. So a step with both reps and a duration had its count dropped and reported in `lost`. Correct for a loose step, but her EMOMs are entirely made of timed AND counted minutes, and the generator now builds them, so a whole section exported as six unlabelled minutes.

detail: USER REPORTED: the generate dialog's report text grew on wide screens, and 'Try another / Cancel / Open in editor' wrapped on a DESKTOP while staying in one row on a phone
error: USER REPORTED: the generate dialog's report text grew on wide screens, and 'Try another / Cancel / Open in editor' wrapped on a DESKTOP while staying in one row on a phone
fix: Added `container: paste / inline-size` to `.generate`, matching `.paste`. cqi now measures the 44rem panel, so `--label-size-sm` sits at its 1rem floor at every width (1.6% of 44rem is 11px) and the 26rem query finally resolves. Side effect: `.paste__title` in the generate dialog drops from ~41px to the 24px the paste dialog already shows.
root_cause: `.generate` never declared a container. `.paste` does (`container: paste / inline-size`), and the panel wears `.paste`'s title, report and actions, all sized in `cqi`: `--label-size-sm: clamp(1rem, 1.6cqi, 1.4rem)`. With no container of its own, cqi measured the LIBRARY screen behind the dialog, so the chips and report text grew with the window while the panel stayed pinned at 44rem — three chips at 1.4rem come to ~724px inside 656px of panel. The same absence meant `@container paste (max-width: 26rem)` had no container to name, so the full-width narrow-phone stack for the actions never fired at all.

detail: USER REPORTED: the exercise dialog's text sizes did not match the generate dialog. Audit found the same missing-container bug in `.exdlg`, `.notice`, `.tray` and `.picker` — every dialog panel in the app except `.paste` and `.generate`.
error: USER REPORTED: the exercise dialog's text sizes did not match the generate dialog. Audit found the same missing-container bug in `.exdlg`, `.notice`, `.tray` and `.picker` — every dialog panel in the app except `.paste` and `.generate`.
fix: Audited every `<dialog>` in the app — six panels: `.paste`, `.generate`, `.notice`, `.exdlg`, `.tray`, `.picker`. Added `container: <name> / inline-size` to the four that lacked one. Wrote the rule as a block comment beside the `--label-size-sm` token in theme.css (the one place a reader of these units lands) and as a Do-Not-Repeat entry. Also gave `.exdlg__title` `var(--size-name)`, so it matches `.paste__title` rather than carrying a third bespoke size.
root_cause: The THIRD sighting of bug-181's cause. `cqi` resolves against the nearest ancestor container; a `<dialog>` is in the top layer but still a child of the screen that opened it, and every screen declares `container-type: inline-size`. So a panel that declares none measures the whole screen behind it. `--label-size-sm: clamp(1rem, 1.6cqi, 1.4rem)`, `--size-name`, `--size-title` and `--size-display` are all cqi, so the panel's legends, chips and titles grew with the window while the panel stayed pinned at its max-width. Invisible at the width a dialog is built at; only shows up on a wide screen, which is why it kept coming back one panel at a time.
